_note: Synthetic bank statements for story MK21. Every amount, reference and holder detail is invented. Nothing here corresponds to a real person or account. Ground truth is included so an import can be scored rather than eyeballed.

difficulties: Debit and credit are separate columns, so the sign must be derived
DD/MM/YYYY is ambiguous with MM/DD/YYYY for days 1-12
Row 4's narrative contains a comma inside a quoted field
CRLF line endings
CP1252 encoding, not UTF-8 — a UTF-8-only reader corrupts the en dash silently
D/M/YY without zero padding, and a two-digit year
Processor prefixes and card suffixes in the description
No balance column, so reconciliation must come from the declared balances
Row 11 has a trailing comma, producing one extra empty field
Row 21 is short, missing amount and balance
ragged.csv.expected_behaviour: Import must report both rows rather than silently padding them

difficulties: The declared closing balance does not match the sum of the transactions
non-reconciling.csv.expected_behaviour: MK21.5's reconciliation check must fail prominently rather than proceeding. A statement that does not reconcile means extraction dropped or misread a transaction, and continuing produces a wrong budget presented with total confidence.

spreadsheet-export.xlsx.date_format: Excel 1900 serial with number format 14; one date is TEXT DD/MM/YYYY
difficulties: Text cells are shared-string indices (as Excel writes them), not inline text
The title in A1 is one shared string stored as two rich-text runs plus a phonetic run that is not part of its text
Three title rows, then row 4 absent: the header is row 5, and rows are sparse
Dates are serial numbers whose type is only in styles.xml (numFmt 14)
Row 9's date is a text cell, DD/MM/YYYY, ambiguous with MM/DD/YYYY
The Reference column is empty on most rows and those cells are omitted, so columns cannot be inferred from cell order
Balance is a formula; only its cached value is a number
Two transactions are genuinely identical (same day, merchant and amount): both are real and neither may be removed as a duplicate
The content stream draws column by column (every date, then every description, then each amount column), so extraction in stream order does not give rows; rows come from each string's position
Transaction 6's description is two text objects side by side, so it must be joined by position, not taken as two fields
DD/MM/YY with a two-digit year, ambiguous with MM/DD/YY for days 1-12
Amounts carry thousands separators (2,163.35)
Two pages: BALANCE CARRIED FORWARD ends page 1 and BALANCE BROUGHT FORWARD opens page 2 with the same figure; neither is a transaction
Some descriptions wrap onto a second line with no date or amount

Misaligned scan: the sheet is rotated 1.75 degrees and shifted, so the lid shows along two edges, and across the page a row falls about 27 pixels, more than the 22-pixel line pitch: without deskewing, an amount lines up with the row below it
No text layer at all: every character needs recognition
Speckle, a vertical streak across the amount columns and two punch holes in the left margin
Uneven ink from character to character, and the paper darkens towards the bottom
Page 1 of 2 only: its transactions reconcile to BALANCE CARRIED FORWARD, not to the statement's closing balance
DD/MM/YY with a two-digit year, and amounts with thousands separators

overlap.description: anz-shaped.csv opens with the same June 2026 transactions that close westpac-shaped.csv, so importing both must deduplicate on date, merchant and amount rather than double-counting. This is the common real-world case when somebody imports several months that share a boundary.
